headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Exam week is almost here. Wiebke lays out the schedule, and the group plans their last days \u2014 when they study, when they meet, when the test starts and what happens afterwards. Every plan hangs on a dative time phrase: am Freitag, seit Wochen, nach der Prüfung.
objective: See which preposition marks which kind of time.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Exam day. Henrike and Henrike wait nervously outside the Pr\u00fcfungsraum, quizzing each other one last time. Then they go in \u2014 and a week later Henrike has news, and three Goethe A1 certificates. The end of the beginning.
objective: See the Goethe A1 exam structure and how to revise for it.

headline: Who are you?
intro: A partner exercise. Two classmates, Lena and Paul, introduce themselves properly — names, where they are from, where they live, their age — and discover they are both new in Berlin.
objective: See the whole chapter at a glance before you begin.

headline: So many questions.
intro: Break time turns into a two-person mini-interview. Sofia fires off the W-questions — where, when, why — and Felix answers, as two classmates turn small talk into real practice.
objective: See the whole chapter at a glance before you begin.

headline: Yes or no?
intro: After class, Ben checks if Mia has time, then finds out how well they actually understand each other — quick-fire yes/no questions, honest answers, and one classic "say that again?" moment.
objective: See the whole chapter at a glance before you begin.

headline: The first checkpoint.
intro: A quick partner checkpoint. Nina interviews Daniel using everything from Chapters 1–7 — name, age, origin — and discovers he comes from a country whose language surprises her.
objective: See what this checkpoint covers and why retrieval matters.

headline: Every day.
intro: Phase 2 begins. Noah asks Clara what she does every day, and the two swap everyday routines — working, learning, cooking, playing — putting the new verb endings straight to work.
objective: See the whole chapter at a glance before you begin.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Season 2 begins. The Goethe A1 certificates have just been handed out, and the same classroom feels new: today is the first day of the A2 course. On the table lie books, bags, phones and photos \u2014 and the group discovers how naturally Germans say whose things they are: Annas Buch, Petra\u2019 Handy, Rohans Tasche.
objective: See the one rule that opens A2: Name + s.

headline: Everything together.
intro: One week before the mock exam, the class runs a warm-up. Runa fires questions; Runa and Runa answer with everything they\u2019ve built this phase \u2014 a Genitiv here, a weil-clause there, a modal in the Pr\u00e4teritum, a comparison with als. Nothing new is taught. This is the sound of nine chapters clicking together.
scene: Aufw\u00e4rmen vor dem Goethe-Mini-Test \u2014 Sprachschule Berlin
objective: Understand the checkpoint and how the mock test is scored.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: It\u2019s the last week before a long break \u2014 Wiebke is leaving for a sailing regatta in Argentina, and the class is planning a small farewell party. Every plan hangs on a condition: if the weather holds, if everyone\u2019s free, whenever Wiebke checks his phone. That makes it the perfect stage for wenn, the word that carries "if", "whenever" and "when" all at once. Wiebke keeps the verb at the end.
scene: Abschiedsplanung vor den Ferien \u2014 Sprachschule Berlin
objective: See wenn do three jobs \u2014 if, whenever, when \u2014 verb always last.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Enya\u2019s sister is getting married on Saturday, and the whole class is caught up in the preparation \u2014 the dress, the cards, the nerves. Everyone is getting ready, hurrying, calming down, looking forward to it. Which makes it the perfect morning for reflexive verbs: sich beeilen, sich freuen, sich anziehen, sich entspannen. Enya keeps the little pronoun \u2014 mich, dich, sich \u2014 in exactly the right place.
scene: Der Morgen vor der Hochzeit \u2014 Sprachschule Berlin
objective: See the mirror-word: reflexive verbs need a pronoun (mich, dich, sich \u2026).

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Frau Nissen\u2019s wallet has vanished somewhere between the bus and the museum, so the morning turns into a small city adventure: a trip to the police, a visit to the Amt about his visa, a coffee across from the station. Every step is a preposition of place and motion \u2014 mit dem Bus, zur Polizei, beim Amt, gegen\u00fcber dem Bahnhof. Frau Nissen keeps the dative endings tidy through all of it.
scene: Ein Vormittag in der Stadt \u2014 Sprachschule Berlin
objective: See the nine always-dative prepositions and what each one does.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Frieda has a new flat and everyone shows up to help move furniture \u2014 which means a whole morning of "put it there / no, it\u2019s already here". The sofa goes against the wall, the lamp between the windows, the boxes into the cellar. Every sentence forces the choice: moving something (wohin? \u2192 Akkusativ) or saying where it now sits (wo? \u2192 Dativ). Frieda turns the chaos into one clean rule.
scene: Umzugstag in Annas neuer Wohnung \u2014 Berlin
objective: See the one test: moving (wohin? \u2192 Akk) vs already there (wo? \u2192 Dat).

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: The class is planning a car-free week for the city, and the office is chaos: plans on the table, maps on the wall, keys stuck in bags, everyone finding a seat. It\u2019s the ideal stage for the position/direction pairs \u2014 stellen vs stehen, legen vs liegen, h\u00e4ngen both ways. Meret keeps asking the one question that picks the verb: Wo, or wohin?
objective: See the pairs: a "put" verb (+Akk) and a "be" verb (+Dat).

headline: Everything together.
intro: Two weeks before the real exam, the class runs its second big warm-up \u2014 and life is providing the material: Frau Wolter needs an ID card from the Beh\u00f6rde, Frau Wolter has a job interview, Frau Wolter is planning a car-free city day. Every answer recycles a whole phase of grammar: a wenn-clause, a reflexive verb, a two-way preposition, a position verb. Nothing new is taught. Frau Wolter just listens for the click.
scene: Aufw\u00e4rmen vor dem Goethe-Mini-Test 2 \u2014 Sprachschule Berlin
objective: See how Phase 2 fits together \u2014 and how the checkpoint works.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: A rainy afternoon, a bandaged finger, and a class full of plans for next year \u2014 the perfect stage for werden. Neele asks what everyone will do, what they\u2019ll become, and what the weather is turning into, and the little verb does all three jobs at once: future, prediction, change of state.
objective: See the one verb, three jobs: future, prediction, change.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: A tourist stops the class outside the school, lost and looking for the Dom. Everyone jumps in with directions \u2014 links, rechts, geradeaus, an der Ampel \u2014 and by the time she finds it, the whole class has drilled every location phrase in real conversation.
scene: Vor der Sprachschule \u2014 eine Touristin fragt nach dem Weg
objective: See what\u2019s new here: phrasing, not grammar.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Between a delayed train, a doctor’s appointment and a mountain of admin, everyone in the group needs information — and nobody wants to sound rude asking for it. Franka shows them the trick: wrap any question in Kannst du mir sagen, …? or Ich weiß nicht, … and it turns polite and indirect, with the verb sliding to the end.
objective: See the frame + W-word/ob + verb-at-the-end pattern.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Monday morning, week two of the A2 course. Everyone comes in full of weekend stories \u2014 a flea market, a rented bicycle, a horse \u2014 and Insa turns it into the perfect Perfekt workout: haben or sein in position 2, Partizip II at the end. You know every rule already. Today it becomes reflex.
objective: See why A2 pauses here: the Perfekt must become automatic.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Solveig is helping at the Bücherei this week — sorting books, running the driving-school desk, and translating for a Gebärdendolmetscher session. Every second conversation starts with was für ein(e): what kind of book, what kind of course, what kind of advice.
objective: See the type-vs-identity idea behind was für ein(e).
